definitions.explanation: The act of waking from sleep or a state of unconsciousness. Used in both literal and figurative senses.

definitions.gloss: arousal; activation of a latent ability or awareness
definitions.explanation: Becoming aware of something previously unrecognized, or the activation of a dormant power or talent. Frequently used in fiction and media to describe a character unlocking hidden abilities.

examples.japanese: {患者|かんじゃ}が{覚醒|かくせい}した。
{麻酔|ますい}からの{覚醒|かくせい}には{時間|じかん}がかかる。
examples.english: It takes time to wake up from anesthesia.

examples.japanese: {手術後|しゅじゅつご}、{覚醒|かくせい}するまで{家族|かぞく}は{待合室|まちあいしつ}で{待|ま}っていた。
examples.english: After the surgery, the family waited in the waiting room until the patient woke up.

examples.japanese: {才能|さいのう}が{覚醒|かくせい}した。
{彼|かれ}はあの{事件|じけん}をきっかけに{政治的|せいじてき}に{覚醒|かくせい}した。
{主人公|しゅじんこう}が{隠|かく}された{力|ちから}に{覚醒|かくせい}する{場面|ばめん}は{物語|ものがたり}のクライマックスだ。
examples.english: The scene where the protagonist awakens to a hidden power is the climax of the story.

notes: Composed of {覚|かく} (perceive, awake) + {醒|せい} (sober, awake). Common collocations: {覚醒|かくせい}する (to awaken), {覚醒|かくせい}{状態|じょうたい} (waking state), {覚醒|かくせい}{作用|さよう} (stimulant effect). The compound {覚醒剤|かくせいざい} refers to stimulant drugs (methamphetamine), which is a controlled substance in Japan — this is a formal/legal term frequently seen in news reports. In medical contexts, {覚醒|かくせい} specifically means regaining consciousness after anesthesia or coma. In gaming and anime, {覚醒|かくせい} is extremely common to describe characters unlocking new powers or transformations.
